facts.claim: Depressive children and adolescents allocated to placebo or active groups had a similar risk to develop adverse events.
facts.quote: There was similar risk for the incidence of adverse events between non-active and active group (global RR 1. 04, 95% CI: 0. 97-1. 11).

facts.claim: The overall magnitude of the nocebo effect in pain was moderate to large, with a range of g=-0.43 to 4.05.
facts.quote: The overall magnitude of the nocebo effect was moderate to large (lowest g=0. 62 [0. 24-1. 01] and highest g=1. 03 [0. 63-1. 43]) and highly variable (range of g=-0. 43 to 4. 05).

facts.claim: Nocebo manipulations make negative expectancy increase with a large effect of g = . 837.
facts.quote: Nocebo manipulations reliably increased negative expectancy with a large effect (g = . 837) and state anxiety with a small effect (g = . 312).

facts.claim: Social learning can contribute to the development of negative health expectations, leading to worsened health outcomes.
facts.quote: While often adaptive, social learning can contribute to the development of negative health expectations, leading to worsened health outcomes, a phenomenon known as the nocebo effect.

facts.claim: Changes in negative expectancy and state anxiety are linked to larger nocebo effects.
facts.quote: Changes in expectancy and state anxiety due to the nocebo manipulation were associated with larger nocebo effects (r = . 376 and . 234, respectively).

facts.claim: Nocebo effects occur when the treatment context generates negative expectancies that trigger the experience or worsening of negative symptoms beyond any effects attributable to the treatment itself.
facts.quote: Nocebo effects occur when the treatment context generates negative expectancies that trigger the experience or worsening of negative symptoms beyond any effects attributable to the treatment itself.

rejected.claim: The pooled estimate of the percentage of placebo-treated patients with at least one adverse event in Menière disease trials was 42. 3%.
rejected.quote: The pooled estimate of the percentage of placebo-treated patients with at least one AE was 42. 3% (95% CI 8. 1% to 16. 3%), in comparison to 53. 8% (95% CI 48. 0% to 59. 5%) for active drug-treated patients.

research.angle: Negative expectations and social learning can trigger real physical symptoms and adverse events that are independent of the actual treatment.
research.verdict: The evidence confirms that nocebo effects are significant and can be reliably induced through verbal suggestions, conditioning, and social learning.
research.caveat: The magnitude of nocebo effects is highly variable and can sometimes be negative, as seen in the range of g=-0.43 to 4.05.
